newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH TRANSFER AND RUMOUR MARKET WARM UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH TRANSFER AND RUMOUR MARKET WARM UP.

text.p: Spain's top clubs are looking for reinforcements as the reopening of the transfer market nears, but one man who won't be going anywhere for the moment is Brazilian striker Ronaldo.
Barcelona club officials on Thursday denied rumours that Paris Saint Germain and AC Milan had made offers for the brilliant 20-year old.
Meanwhile arch-rivals Real Madrid have moved a step closer to signing Sampdoria's French international Christian Karembeu and young Monaco star Thierry Henry.
"Sooner rather than later Karembeu and Henry will play for Real," said club chairman Lorenzo Sanz on his return from a trip to Geneva to negotiate with Karembeu's representatives.
Despite Sanz's remarks, reports suggest that neither player is likely to make the move before the end of the season.
But the market for rumours is always open.

Press speculation over Real's interest in Brazilian players has also intensified after a videotape of a match between Santos and Internacional was seen in the back seat of a car driven by reserve coach Italo Galbiati.
Several newspapers published a list of targetted players as a result of the sighting.
A source at the club downplayed the incident.
"There are 17,000 videos like that," he said.
But another Brazilian, World Cup striker Bebeto, looks increasingly likely to return to Spain, a place he calls his 'second home'.
Sevilla chairman Jose Maria Gonzalez will travel to Brazil if Flamengo lose this weekend to Palmeiras and fail to qualify for the final section of the Brazilian championship.
"The operation is in the final straight. We have reached an agreement in principle both with the player and (Flamengo)." said Gonzalez.

Gonzalez added that another South American at Sevilla -- Argentine midfielder Christian Colusso -- could be sent back to Rosario Central because of the discovery of forged signatures in transfer documentation.
Sevilla have already suspended payment of the money still owed to Rosario because of discrepancies between the contracts held by the Spanish and Argentine clubs.
Gonzalez also confirmed Sevilla's interest in Croatian midfielder Robert Prosinecki, who has been the hot potato of Spanish football since signing for Real Madrid in 1991.
Prosinecki failed to reproduce the form that had made him a European Cup winner at Red Star Belgrade, and he went on loan to Oviedo before joining Barcelona, where he has hardly played.
"My situation at Barcelona is unsustainable," said Prosinecki in an article published in the sports daily As on Thursday.

Prosinecki hopes to move in December, when the Spanish transfer market reopens. Under the country's system, only players who have made four appearances or less since the beginning of the season are allowed to change clubs.

In some cases players are not picked so as to maintain their value in the transfer market. Barcelona are thought to have given coach Bobby Robson orders not to use Angel Cuellar so the international striker can be transferred back to his old club, Real Betis.
